explain.html:
Un día en Madrid1:25

No te preocupes, ya me las apañaré.

Don’t worry, I’ll manage somehow.

a·pa·ñár·se·las

/a.paˈɲaɾ.se.las/verb, reflexive

to manage on your own, somehow

Usually: to fix or patch something up (apañar)

In this scene

She’s brushing off the offer: “don’t worry, I’ll sort it out myself”. It sounds relaxed and a little proud.

“Apañárselas” means to get by with what you have. The “las” doesn’t point at anything; it’s part of the phrase.

Tips

Why here

She was just asked if she needs help, and answers with “no te preocupes” first.

Another way to say it

Ya me las arreglaré.

Same meaning, heard all over the Spanish-speaking world; “apañar” sounds more like Spain.

Other meanings

to tidy up · to dress up a little

Lines before

¿Seguro que no necesitas ayuda? Are you sure you don’t need help?

panel.html:
Sintel1:58

¿Qué te trae a la tierra de los guardianes?

What brings you to the land of the guardians?

tra·er

/tɾaˈeɾ/verb

What brings you to the land of the guardians?

Usually: to bring or carry; here, to bring someone somewhere for a reason

In this scene

“What brings you to the land of the guardians?” asks why she has come there. After she thanks the speaker, they use it to invite her to explain her purpose. The wording is conversational and curious; “te” addresses her informally, though the question itself doesn’t establish how warm or serious the speaker sounds.

“¿Qué te trae a…?” is a natural way to ask what reason or purpose brought someone to a place; it doesn’t literally ask what is carrying them.

Tips

Why here

It follows her “Gracias” and a pause-marked “Entonces...”, leading into a question about her reason for being there.

Other meanings

to wear or have on · to cause or result in
